name: TMA (cp.async.bulk.tensor): hardware address generation and predication for global->shared copies
arithmetic_intensity: TMA reduces register pressure and address-computation work in the copy path, which is what allows larger tiles and therefore more FLOPs per byte moved from HBM. The mechanism from the PTX ISA: cp.async.bulk.tensor is a non-blocking instruction that initiates an asynchronous copy of tensor data from .src to .dst, with completion tracked either by an mbarrier (mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes) or by a bulk-group. It is the instruction that makes a tensor map (a host- or device-built descriptor of strides and extents) the unit of transfer, so the hardware does index math and bounds predication. That register saving is the quantitative claim: freed registers mean larger tiles, and larger tiles amortize each HBM byte over more MACs. Three hard scoping facts from the ISA: (1) the .shared::cluster.global direction 'is optimized for' sm_90a/sm_100a/sm_100f/sm_103a/sm_103f/sm_107a/sm_107f/sm_110a/sm_110f and 'may have substantially reduced performance on other targets' - so a cluster-scoped TMA copy on a non-Hopper-plus part is a trap; (2) sub-byte types are NOT supported for .shared::cluster.global on sm_120a, which constrains a cluster-mapped FP4 pipeline on consumer Blackwell; (3) tcgen05.commit gained a .multicast::cluster::32b qualifier and mbarrier.expect_tx gained the same, i.e. multicast completion is a 5th-gen feature. cp.async.bulk.prefetch additionally has a .level::eviction_priority qualifier and applypriority.async.bulk lets the kernel hint L2 eviction policy - the same idea Marlin uses with its immediate-eviction cache policy.
scales_with: tile size enabled by the freed registers
data element size (sub-byte types restricted on sm_120a)
workarounds: Use a tensor map descriptor instead of per-thread address arithmetic so registers are not spent on indexing
Pair TMA with mbarrier (or bulk_group) completion rather than polling
Target the arch-specific list for cluster-direction copies, or measure before assuming parity on other targets
Use applypriority.async.bulk / eviction-priority prefetch for streaming weights that are read once
Fall back to cp.async (Ampere+) where TMA's arch target does not match
notes: cp.async (Ampere and later) is the simpler predecessor: it is per-thread async global->shared copy with commit_group/wait_group pipelining, and it is what pre-Hopper kernels used. TMA is the Hopper-generation replacement where a whole tensor tile moves by descriptor. ThunderKittens names both as the primitives it hides: 'Hide latencies with asynchronous copies and address generation with TMA'. The ISA also documents swizzling patterns for the SMEM destination and notes one copy sub-mode's swizzle is legal only when cp.async.bulk.tensor's direction is .shared::cluster.global or .shared::cta.global - a layout constraint that interacts with any 4-bit or FP8 tile where bank conflicts are already the problem.
